{
  "judgment": "Not the forced-seller story here because this registry supplies no spinoff evidence for this ticker. There is no parent, distribution ratio, record date or distribution date. With no distribution recorded, no holder received shares they were obliged or inclined to dump, so the forced-seller and indifferent-seller criteria have nothing to rest on. That says only that this registry carries no spinoff record; it does not establish that the company has never been spun off. For the same reason, nothing documents debt raised, cash sent to a parent, retained liabilities or restrictions, so the load-pushed-in criterion cannot be credited. The parent-motive criterion is likewise empty. No insider report was saved, so open-market buying after any distribution is unestablished rather than shown to be absent.\n\nOn price against value, the worksheet could not compute the low case or the mid case. The code compared the supplied closing price against an empty low case and reached no result, so cheapness on value is unproven, not disproven. The missing inputs are an actual shares-outstanding count and a matched cash and total-debt balance. The operating inputs are present: net income [fact:after_tax_earnings], depreciation and amortization [fact:depreciation_and_amortization] and capital expenditures [fact:capital_spending], all from the annual report's statements of operations and cash flows. So owner cash flow has its building blocks, but there is nothing to divide it by.\n\nEvery criterion scoring zero here reflects missing spinoff and insider evidence, not a finding that sellers are absent or that the stock is dear. As supplied, this is an ordinary listed company, and no special-situation selling explains its price.",
  "next_filing_trigger": "If the next quarterly report's cover page states an actual shares-outstanding count, and its condensed consolidated balance sheet states cash and total debt explicitly, the worksheet can compute the low case. If the price then sits at or below the low case, the price-against-value criterion would move off zero. Separately, any insider report showing open-market purchases would give the insider criterion something to score, though without a distribution it would not restore a spinoff thesis.",
  "insight": "The annual report's cash flow statement shows depreciation and amortization [fact:depreciation_and_amortization] running above capital expenditures [fact:capital_spending]. Owner cash flow as the worksheet defines it would therefore sit above reported net income [fact:after_tax_earnings], not below it. Part of that gap may be amortization of acquired intangibles rather than wear on assets the business must replace, so the excess should be confirmed before it is treated as durable cash."
}
